title: Sixth Word Five Degrees Of Profit From Selling The Trust

questions.question: What is the first gain mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A temporary life becomes lasting when it is used for Allah’s sake.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the result of giving one’s life to Allah?
questions.answer: It says that what seems to pass away will produce lasting results in the next life.

questions.question: What image is used to show that short moments can lead to lasting reward?
questions.answer: The image of seeds that later grow into beautiful blossoms.

questions.question: Besides the eternal world, where else do those good results show a comforting side?
questions.answer: In the Intermediate Realm.

questions.question: What is the second gain in this trade?
questions.answer: Paradise is given as the reward.

questions.question: What is the third gain about a person’s abilities and body parts?
questions.answer: Their worth becomes greatly increased.

questions.question: What example is given first to explain this third gain?
questions.answer: The intelligence.

questions.question: What happens to intelligence when it is used only for the nafs?
questions.answer: It becomes harmful and fills a person with sorrow about the past and fear about the future.

questions.question: Why does the passage say some sinful people run to drinking or useless fun?
questions.answer: They want to escape the pain and pressure caused by their troubled minds.

questions.question: What does intelligence become when it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a means for understanding mercy and wisdom and guiding a person toward eternal happiness.

questions.question: What is the second sense used as an example?
questions.answer: The eye.

questions.question: What happens to the eye when it is used for selfish desires?
questions.answer: It falls to a low use by chasing passing beauty and desire.

questions.question: What higher role does the eye have when used within Allah’s limits?
questions.answer: It becomes a way to observe creation with meaning and notice Allah’s signs and mercy.

questions.question: What is the third example given after intelligence and the eye?
questions.answer: The tongue and the sense of taste.

questions.question: What happens to taste when it is used only for the stomach and the nafs?
questions.answer: It drops to a very low job, serving only appetite.

questions.question: What does the tongue become when used for the Generous Provider?
questions.answer: It becomes a thankful and skillful servant recognizing Allah’s mercy in provision.

questions.question: What are readers told to do with the other limbs and abilities not named one by one?
questions.answer: Compare them to these examples and understand the same rule applies.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of nature does a believer gain?
questions.answer: A character fit for Paradise.

questions.question: What kind of nature does an unbeliever gain?
questions.answer: A character fit for Hell.

questions.question: What is the main reason believers and unbelievers end up with different values?
questions.answer: The believer uses Allah’s trust in the way Allah allows, while the unbeliever misuses it for the nafs.

questions.question: What human condition is described at the start of the fourth gain?
questions.answer: Human beings are helpless, needy, and weak while facing many troubles.

questions.question: What happens if a person does not rely on Allah and trust Him?
questions.answer: The person’s inner life stays disturbed and full of pain, regret, and useless suffering.

questions.question: What strong warning is given about what this inner suffering can do to a person?
questions.answer: It can overwhelm the person or reduce him to a beast-like state.

questions.question: What is the fifth gain connected to worship done by the body and senses?
questions.answer: Its reward will come back to the person as fruits of Paradise when they are most needed.

questions.question: Who agrees on this fifth gain according to the passage?
questions.answer: People of spiritual insight who have seen the truth of things.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the main message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: If a person uses life and abilities for Allah, those temporary trusts turn into eternal gain and reward.

questions.question: Into what does the passage say temporary property is changed in the first gain?
questions.answer: It is changed into something everlasting.

questions.question: What condition must be met for a fading life to gain eternity?
questions.answer: It must be given to Allah and used for His sake.

questions.question: How are the moments of life pictured before their lasting results appear?
questions.answer: They seem to disappear like seeds that are buried.

questions.question: What comes out of those moments in the life to come?
questions.answer: Lasting blessings and joy.

questions.question: What reward is named as the second gain?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What broad idea is taught in the third gain?
questions.answer: Every human ability becomes far more valuable when used for Allah.

questions.question: When intelligence serves the nafs, what two time-related pains does it bring?
questions.answer: Sadness about what is gone and fear about what is coming.

questions.question: What does this teach about the mind when it is misused?
questions.answer: A great gift can turn into a source of harm.

questions.question: When intelligence is used for Allah, what does it help open?
questions.answer: It helps a person understand the hidden treasures of mercy and wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What future does such guided intelligence prepare a person for?
questions.answer: Everlasting happiness.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can the eye be misused?
questions.answer: By looking at temporary attractions for selfish desire.

questions.question: What does the eye become when it is used rightly?
questions.answer: A way to read the signs in creation and witness Allah’s artistry.

questions.question: What sweet image is used for the eye in its proper use?
questions.answer: It is compared to a bee taking from flowers in a garden of mercy.

questions.question: What part of the body is connected with the sense of taste?
questions.answer: The tongue.

questions.question: What low level does taste fall to when it is used only for appetite?
questions.answer: It becomes like a servant of the stomach.

questions.question: What honorable role does taste have when used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a thankful inspector of divine generosity in food and provision.

questions.question: Why does the passage directly call on intelligence, eye, and tongue?
questions.answer: To make the reader notice the huge difference between low use and noble use.

questions.question: What should a reader conclude after comparing the other limbs with these examples?
questions.answer: All human abilities can rise or fall depending on how they are used.

questions.question: How does faith affect the way a believer treats the trusts given by the Creator?
questions.answer: Faith leads the believer to use them in Allah’s service and within His limits.

questions.question: What is betrayal of trust in this passage?
questions.answer: Using Allah’s gifts for the nafs instead of for their true purpose.

questions.question: What three qualities of man are highlighted in the fourth gain?
questions.answer: Helplessness, poverty of means, and weakness.

questions.question: What makes the burden of life especially hard for such a person?
questions.answer: Human needs are many and misfortunes are numerous.

questions.question: What brings peace to such a weak and needy person?
questions.answer: Relying on Allah, trusting Him, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: What happens to a person who refuses that reliance?
questions.answer: The person is choked by useless suffering, pain, and regret.

questions.question: According to the fifth gain, when will the reward of worship be especially important?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: In what form will that reward appear?
questions.answer: As the fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: What change happens to a short worldly life in the first profit?
questions.answer: It gains an everlasting result.

questions.question: Why does the passage call worldly property and life temporary?
questions.answer: Because they do not stay and are fading away.

questions.question: What makes these temporary things last forever?
questions.answer: Using them for Allah and returning them to His service.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of seeds and flowers?
questions.answer: Small acts in this life can grow into great reward in the next life.

questions.question: What is offered as the exchange in the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to each body part and sense in the third profit?
questions.answer: Its value becomes much greater.

questions.question: Which human faculty is explained first in detail?
questions.answer: The intelligence.

questions.question: How does misused intelligence hurt a person emotionally?
questions.answer: It loads the person with grief and fear.

questions.question: What behavior is mentioned as an escape from that pain?
questions.answer: Turning to intoxicants or pointless entertainment.

questions.question: What does this suggest about sinful pleasures?
questions.answer: They may be used to avoid inner pain, not solve it.

questions.question: How does intelligence change when used on Allah’s behalf?
questions.answer: It becomes a guide that opens understanding and leads toward eternal joy.

questions.question: What does the passage present the eye as when used correctly?
questions.answer: A viewer of Allah’s signs and artistry in the world.

questions.question: What lowers the eye from that high role?
questions.answer: Using it to chase passing beauty for selfish desire.

questions.question: How is the tongue lowered when it serves only appetite?
questions.answer: It becomes nothing more than a servant for the stomach.

questions.question: How is the tongue elevated when it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a thankful recognizer of His mercy in provision.

questions.question: What are readers invited to compare after these three examples?
questions.answer: All the rest of their faculties and limbs.

questions.question: What result does this comparison lead to for a believer?
questions.answer: A nature suited for Paradise.

questions.question: What result does it lead to for an unbeliever?
questions.answer: A nature suited for Hell.

questions.question: What is the key difference in how the two use what they were given?
questions.answer: One uses it faithfully under Allah’s guidance, and the other uses it selfishly.

questions.question: What reality about human life is stressed in the fourth profit?
questions.answer: Humans cannot handle life well by themselves because they are weak and needy.

questions.question: What three actions toward Allah are named as the right response?
questions.answer: Relying on Him, trusting Him, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: What happens inside a person who does not do this?
questions.answer: The conscience remains restless and overwhelmed.

questions.question: What two severe outcomes are mentioned for that person’s state?
questions.answer: Being drowned in pain and regret, or sinking to an animal-like level.

questions.question: Who confirms the truth of the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Spiritually awakened people who have witnessed reality.

questions.question: What will be returned as fruits of Paradise?
questions.answer: The reward for worship and glorifying Allah done by one’s limbs and faculties.

questions.question: What overall choice does the passage put before the reader?
questions.answer: Whether to use Allah’s trusts for Him and gain eternal reward or misuse them and fall low.

questions.question: What is the first benefit of giving one’s temporary life and property to Allah?
questions.answer: They become a source of everlasting gain.

questions.question: What happens to actions done for Allah even if they seem to disappear in this world?
questions.answer: They remain and bear fruit in the next life.

questions.question: Which two places are connected to the good results of such actions?
questions.answer: The eternal realm and the Intermediate Realm.

questions.question: What is the second benefit named clearly in the passage?
questions.answer: Receiving Paradise.

questions.question: What central claim is made in the third benefit?
questions.answer: Human powers and senses become far more valuable when directed to Allah.

questions.question: What is intelligence compared to at the start of its example?
questions.answer: A useful instrument.

questions.question: What turns intelligence into something harmful?
questions.answer: Using it for the nafs instead of for Allah.

questions.question: What burdens does such misused intelligence put on a person?
questions.answer: The pain of old sorrows and the fear of what may come.

questions.question: How does the passage explain some sinful people’s search for distraction?
questions.answer: They try to flee the distress caused by their own minds.

questions.question: What noble role can intelligence play when used rightly?
questions.answer: It can unlock understanding of creation and guide a person to eternal happiness.

questions.question: Why is the eye important according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is a way for the spirit to look at the world.

questions.question: What wrong use of the eye is criticized?
questions.answer: Looking at short-lived attractions with selfish desire.

questions.question: What good use of the eye is praised?
questions.answer: Seeing Allah’s signs, art, and mercy in creation.

questions.question: What body part is linked with taste in the next example?
questions.answer: The tongue.

questions.question: What is wrong with using the tongue only for the stomach?
questions.answer: It lowers a noble gift to serving appetite alone.

questions.question: What is right about using the tongue for Allah?
questions.answer: It allows a person to appreciate and thank Allah for His provision.

questions.question: What thinking skill are readers asked to use after these examples?
questions.answer: Comparison.

questions.question: What should they compare?
questions.answer: Their other limbs and faculties with the examples already explained.

questions.question: What is the believer’s value based on in this comparison?
questions.answer: Faithful use of Allah’s trust within His boundaries.

questions.question: What is the unbeliever’s problem in this comparison?
questions.answer: Misusing the trust for instinct and selfish desire.

questions.question: What facts about human beings support the fourth benefit?
questions.answer: People are helpless, poor in resources, weak, and surrounded by troubles.

questions.question: What protects a person from being crushed by life according to the passage?
questions.answer: Dependence on Allah through trust and submission.

questions.question: What happens if someone refuses that dependence?
questions.answer: The person suffers inwardly with regret, pain, and pointless torment.

questions.question: What lower state may that person fall into?
questions.answer: A beast-like condition.

questions.question: What do spiritually enlightened people agree upon in the fifth benefit?
questions.answer: Worship done by one’s body and faculties will return as reward in Paradise.

questions.question: Why is that reward especially precious?
questions.answer: It will come when a person needs it most.

questions.question: In the first profit, what happens to life that is fading away?
questions.answer: It is turned into eternal gain.

questions.question: For whose sake must life be spent for this change to happen?
questions.answer: For Allah’s sake.

questions.question: What do the passing moments of life become in the hereafter?
questions.answer: They become lasting fruits of blessing and happiness.

questions.question: What extra comfort is mentioned besides their eternal reward?
questions.answer: They also have a bright and comforting aspect in the Intermediate Realm.

questions.question: What is received in return according to the second profit?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What does the third profit teach about the human body and senses?
questions.answer: Their value rises greatly when they are used in the right way.

questions.question: What is the danger of using intelligence for selfish purposes?
questions.answer: It turns into a source of distress, fear, and harm.

questions.question: Which two directions of time trouble a selfishly used mind?
questions.answer: The past and the future.

questions.question: What wrong coping methods are mentioned for those hurt by such misuse?
questions.answer: Intoxicants and shallow amusement.

questions.question: What does intelligence become when it serves its true Owner?
questions.answer: A guide that opens deep understanding and leads to eternal joy.

questions.question: What temptation makes the eye fall from its proper place?
questions.answer: Chasing a few temporary beauties out of desire.

questions.question: What honorable work does the eye do when used for Allah?
questions.answer: It studies creation and witnesses Allah’s miracles and mercy.

questions.question: What is the problem with using the tongue only for taste and appetite?
questions.answer: It reduces a noble sense to serving the stomach.

questions.question: What honorable description is given to taste when used properly?
questions.answer: It becomes a thankful supervisor recognizing Allah’s mercy in provision.

questions.question: What should a reader understand by comparing all the other faculties to these examples?
questions.answer: Every faculty can either rise in honor or sink in disgrace.

questions.question: What makes the believer worthy of Paradise?
questions.answer: Using Allah’s trust faithfully and within His limits.

questions.question: What makes the unbeliever fit for Hell?
questions.answer: Betraying the trust by using it for the nafs.

questions.question: What is said about man’s ability to handle hardships on his own?
questions.answer: He is too weak, needy, and helpless to manage by himself.

questions.question: What is the healthy response to this weakness?
questions.answer: To depend on Allah, trust Him, and submit to Him.

questions.question: What happens to the conscience without that trust?
questions.answer: It stays troubled and weighed down.

questions.question: What kinds of pain are mentioned in that troubled condition?
questions.answer: Torment, regret, and sorrow that do not help.

questions.question: What extreme moral decline is mentioned as a possible result?
questions.answer: Becoming beast-like.

questions.question: Who are said to agree about the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Those with spiritual illumination and insight into reality.

questions.question: What actions are included in the reward described in the fifth profit?
questions.answer: Worship and glorifying Allah done by the body’s members and instruments.

questions.question: When will those rewards be presented?
questions.answer: At the time of greatest need.

questions.question: In what form will they be presented?
questions.answer: As fruits of Paradise.

questions.question: What is the first of the five profits in the passage?
questions.answer: Temporary possessions and life gain an everlasting result when devoted to Allah.

questions.question: What causes a fading human life to become linked to eternity?
questions.answer: Spending it for Allah and giving it to Him.

questions.question: What natural example helps explain how brief deeds can have lasting results?
questions.answer: Seeds that later grow into flowers.

questions.question: What does this example teach about good deeds?
questions.answer: Even if they seem to disappear now, they can produce lasting reward later.

questions.question: What is the second profit named in a short and direct way?
questions.answer: Paradise is given in return.

questions.question: What is the main point of the third profit?
questions.answer: Each faculty and sense becomes far more precious when used for Allah.

questions.question: Which faculty is discussed first to show this point?
questions.answer: The intelligence.

questions.question: What does the mind become when it follows the nafs?
questions.answer: A harmful burden that fills a person with pain and fear.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest this harmful state may drive people toward?
questions.answer: Escaping into drinking or empty entertainment.

questions.question: What does the mind become when it is used for its true Owner?
questions.answer: A key that opens understanding of mercy and wisdom.

questions.question: What destination does such a rightly used mind help prepare for?
questions.answer: Eternal happiness.

questions.question: What sense is explained through the image of a window for the spirit?
questions.answer: The eye.

questions.question: What lowers the eye to a shameful use?
questions.answer: Using it to seek passing beauty for lustful desire.

questions.question: What raises the eye to a noble use?
questions.answer: Using it within Allah’s limits to observe His signs in creation.

questions.question: What organ is connected to the sense of taste in the third example?
questions.answer: The tongue.

questions.question: How is taste dishonored when it serves only the stomach?
questions.answer: It is reduced to a lowly job centered on appetite.

questions.question: How is taste honored when used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes a thankful recognizer of divine mercy in food.

questions.question: What conclusion should be made about the rest of the human faculties?
questions.answer: They also rise or fall depending on whether they serve Allah or the nafs.

questions.question: What kind of inner nature does faith build in a believer?
questions.answer: One suitable for Paradise.

questions.question: Why does the unbeliever end up with a different inner nature?
questions.answer: Because he misuses the trust for selfish instinct instead of Allah’s purpose.

questions.question: What human weakness is highlighted at the beginning of the fourth profit?
questions.answer: People are helpless, needy, weak, and surrounded by hardships.

questions.question: What three attitudes toward Allah protect a person in that condition?
questions.answer: Reliance, trust, and submission.

questions.question: What is the result if a person does not turn to Allah in this way?
questions.answer: The person lives with a disturbed conscience and choking inner pain.

questions.question: What two expressions describe how serious that suffering can become?
questions.answer: It can overwhelm the person like intoxication or drag him down to a beast-like level.

questions.question: According to the fifth profit, who confirms the truth of this reward?
questions.answer: The spiritually elect who have seen reality unveiled.

questions.question: What is promised for worship done through one’s limbs and faculties?
questions.answer: It will return as the fruits of Paradise when the person needs it most.
